strings.name: Joe Biden
strings.summary: Biden represented Delaware in the Senate before becoming vice president and the 46th US president. He advanced investment in infrastructure, semiconductors and clean energy and influenced domestic policy and alliances. His criminal justice record, Afghanistan withdrawal and Gaza policy drew criticism. After a debate intensified concerns over his age and fitness, he ended his 2024 reelection campaign and left office in 2025.
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through 13 November 2026. Selected milestones do not constitute an exhaustive record of all news or controversies.
strings.influence.rationale: Served for decades as a senator and became US president; his infrastructure, industrial-policy and foreign-policy decisions have had global influence.
strings.facts.fact-01.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.fact-02.label: Education
strings.facts.fact-02.value: University of Delaware, bachelor’s degree (1965); Syracuse University, law degree (1968)
strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Public investment legislation
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: Signed infrastructure, semiconductor and clean energy legislation that expanded long-term federal investment.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: A long public career
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: Served thirty-six years in the Senate, followed by eight years as vice president and one presidential term.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Left the presidency
strings.timeline.event-01.text: Donald Trump succeeded him; his industrial investment, inflation record and foreign policy remained contested.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Ended his reelection campaign
strings.timeline.event-02.text: Concerns over his fitness after debating Trump and pressure within his party prompted his withdrawal.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Signed the Inflation Reduction Act
strings.timeline.event-03.text: The law funded clean energy and changed prescription drug policy; its name did not imply an immediate fall in inflation.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Signed the infrastructure law
strings.timeline.event-04.text: The bipartisan law expanded investment in roads, bridges, broadband and other infrastructure.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Afghanistan withdrawal controversy
strings.timeline.event-05.text: Ended the long US military presence, while the chaotic Kabul evacuation and Taliban takeover drew sharp criticism.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Became US president
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Took office after winning the 2020 election, confronting the pandemic and deep political divisions.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Became vice president
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Elected alongside Barack Obama and later reelected, serving until 2017.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Advanced criminal justice laws
strings.timeline.event-08.text: Helped advance the crime law and Violence Against Women Act; the former’s punitive approach later drew criticism.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Elected to the Senate
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Won election at twenty-nine and began his long Senate career representing Delaware the following year.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Completed his legal education
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Earned a Syracuse law degree after graduating from the University of Delaware in 1965.
strings.timeline.event-11.title: Born in Scranton
strings.timeline.event-11.text: Born in Pennsylvania and later moved with his family to Delaware.
